verificationCriteria: When the app is configured for live preview and the CMS sends a preview signal for a page entry, the rendered page displays the draft content of that entry — including its heading, body text, and media assets.
When the CMS sends an updated preview signal for an entry currently being displayed, the page re-renders with the revised draft content without a full browser page reload.

When the CMS sends a preview signal for an entry that includes referenced entries (e.g., line colors for service updates, blog categories for blog listing pages, station data for station finder pages), the page renders those referenced entries as visible content within the respective sections.

notes: Novel feature: Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. The contentstack SDK (already installed) supports live_preview in its Config interface with { host, management_token, enable }, and the Stack class exposes livePreviewQuery(). However @contentstack/live-preview-utils (which provides livePreviewInit and onEntryChange for React) is NOT installed and must be added as a new dependency. Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time, so VCs are written to our side of the boundary — verifying our code registers the callback, passes the correct config, and re-renders when that callback fires.

notes: Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with helpful notes about the SDK shape and the missing @contentstack/live-preview-utils dependency. I built the full AC list from scratch based on codebase examination. Key findings from reading the actual files: (1) contentstack.ts initializes Stack with options object and calls Stack.setHost() separately — the live_preview config must be added to the options passed to contentstack.Stack(); (2) ContentstackContext.tsx uses useMemo keyed on defaultContent — the live preview callback must trigger a state update that causes re-render; (3) _app.tsx wraps the app in ContentstackProvider with defaultContent={content} from pageProps; (4) .env.local.sample has a Contentstack section but no live preview vars; (5) @contentstack/live-preview-utils is confirmed absent from package.json. I added AC-2 (graceful degradation when env vars absent), AC-7 (protected pages limitation from story description), AC-8 (SSR must not use draft content), AC-9 (host unreachable edge case), AC-11 (client-only initialization), and AC-12 (CSP considerations) as edge-case/error-handling/security criteria that openspec's notes did not cover.

after.description: AS a Content Author, I WANT to preview draft entries in CMS, SO THAT I can see how content will be shown on the website. This requires integrating Contentstack's Live Preview SDK for a Next.js CSR (Pages Router) application: adding a live_preview config block (enable, host) to the Stack initialization in src/services/contentstack.ts, installing and initializing @contentstack/live-preview-utils on the client side in src/pages/_app.tsx, wiring the onEntryChange callback to trigger a re-render through the existing ContentstackContext/useContent pipeline (note: per Contentstack documentation, onEntryChange takes no arguments — the re-render relies on the SDK's internal state update, not a callback parameter), and documenting the live_preview.enable and live_preview.host environment variables in .env.local.sample. Custom preview URL patterns are configured in the Contentstack dashboard (Settings > Stack > Live Preview), not via application environment variables. Limitation: Protected pages may not be previewable because the authentication gate cannot be bypassed by preview parameters.

verificationCriteria: When the Live Preview SDK signals a draft entry, the page renders the draft field values — such as updated text, headings, and images — corresponding to the unpublished state of that entry.
When the Live Preview feature is not active, the page renders all published content — headings, text blocks, images, and layout — completely and without visible errors.
When the Live Preview SDK signals a change to a draft entry, the page updates to show the new draft content without a full browser page reload.
When the preview environment is configured and Live Preview is active, the page renders all content and layout without visible rendering errors, broken elements, or missing sections.
When the documented preview environment variables are set to valid values, the page loads successfully and displays draft content for entries with unpublished changes.
For pages that require authentication, draft content preview may not render even when the Live Preview SDK signals a draft entry update.

KEY RESOLUTION of documentation contradictions: (1) The Contentstack docs state onEntryChange 'does not take any arguments' — the re-render must rely on the SDK's internal state update mechanism, not a callback parameter carrying the updated entry. VCs assert observable re-render behavior, not callback signatures. (2) Custom preview URLs are configured in the Contentstack dashboard UI, not via application environment variables. However, the live_preview.enable and live_preview.host properties on the Stack initialization ARE app-side configuration that can be driven by env vars. VCs about env vars are scoped to these Stack-init properties only, not to dashboard-side preview URL configuration. The upexpress codeline lacks .env.local.sample; env var documentation VCs apply only to codelines where that file exists (gotransit, metrolinx).

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria with valuable notes about documentation contradictions. I built all ACs from scratch informed by those notes and by direct codebase examination. KEY FINDINGS FROM CODE REVIEW: (1) src/services/contentstack.ts exports a `contentstack.Config` options object and a `Stack` created from it — the live_preview block must be added to this options object. (2) ContentstackContext is a simple createContext with no state setter — the onEntryChange callback must trigger a context value update for useContent consumers to re-render. (3) _app.tsx currently has no ContentstackContext provider and no live preview SDK initialization. (4) @contentstack/live-preview-utils is installed in node_modules but NOT declared in package.json — AC-7 addresses this. (5) The SDK's onEntryChange takes a callback of type OnEntryChangeCallback (no arguments) confirming openspec's note that re-render relies on SDK internal state, not callback parameters. (6) .env.local.sample exists for metrolinx and gotransit but NOT for upexpress — AC-6 is scoped accordingly. (7) No existing live preview code was found anywhere in the codebase (search returned zero matches). AC-5 (SSR safety) and AC-8 (SDK failure graceful degradation) address the most likely integration pitfalls. AC-9 formalizes the protected-page limitation from the story description. AC-11 covers the edge case where enable is true but host is missing. AC-12 ensures backward compatibility since the context interface must change to support re-render.
